newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai securities exchange to cut trading fees.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai securities exchange to cut trading fees.

text.p: The Shanghai Securities Exchange will cut various trading fees from October 3 to improve activity, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the commission for share and fund trading would be lowered to 0.35 percent from 0.4 percent, while the handling charge would be lowered to 0.012 percent from 0.015 percent.
It said the bourse planned further measures to reduce trading costs.
"These measures will help to further reduce investors' costs and enliven the market," the newspaper said.
The Shanghai exchange's position as China's prime stock market has come under attack in recent months with Shenzhen in the south rapidly expanding its business.
Brokers say the Shanghai exchange has been under pressure from members to take measures to regain the initiative.
